Pros:
- Highest static pressure and CFM among conventional 5015 blowers
- Industrial-grade ball bearing — rated 50,000+ hours MTTF
- Consistent specs — Delta is a major OEM supplier to server and telecom industry
- Significantly better overhang performance vs GDStime at aggressive print speeds
- Available through Digi-Key and Mouser — not dependent on AliExpress supply chain
Cons:
- Loud: ~50 dBA at full speed — significant increase over GDStime and Sunon
- Overkill for standard-speed printing — advantage only shows at 200+ mm/s
- More expensive (~$18–25)
- High static pressure curve means Klipper fan config may need tuning to avoid unnecessary noise at idle
Name: Delta Electronics BFB0524HH 5015
Description: The Delta BFB0524HH is the maximum-performance 5015 blower for Voron toolheads. Its industrial ball-bearing construction and high-pressure impeller design give it roughly double the static pressure of the GDStime BOM fan. The trade-off is noise — at full speed it’s noticeably louder than either GDStime or Sunon. Community consensus: worth it for high-speed printing (300+ mm/s), overkill for standard builds. Available from proper electronics distributors, not just AliExpress.
Verdict Label: Highest static pressure 5015 — best for high-speed demanding prints

Pros:
- MagLev (magnetic levitation) bearing — no contact wear, extremely long lifespan
- Quieter than GDStime at equivalent PWM settings (~35 dBA vs ~42 dBA)
- Higher static pressure than sleeve-bearing alternatives at same RPM
- Consistent spec performance across batches — Sunon is a proper Taiwanese OEM
- Drop-in 5015 replacement: same mounting holes, same connector pinout
Cons:
- 3–4× the price of GDStime (~$12–15 vs ~$4)
- Not on official Voron BOM — requires a conscious upgrade choice
- MagLev has slightly lower peak static pressure than Delta BFB0524HH ball-bearing variant
Name: Sunon MF50151VX 5015
Description: The Sunon MF50151VX (MagLev series) is the community’s most-recommended 5015 upgrade from the GDStime BOM fan. MagLev bearing means zero sliding contact — the rotor floats magnetically, delivering longer lifespan and noticeably quieter operation. At ~$12–15 it’s 3–4× more expensive than GDStime but less than a Delta, making it the pragmatic middle ground. Flows slightly more air than GDStime at the same PWM percentage and does so more quietly.
Verdict Label: Go-to upgrade — quieter, longer-lasting, better consistency than GDStime

Pros:
- Compact 40×20mm blower format fits toolheads where a 5015 won’t
- Delta ball bearing — industrial lifespan, consistent specs
- Higher static pressure than axial fans in the same size class
- Sourced through Digi-Key/Mouser — not AliExpress dependent
Cons:
Lower airflow volume than any 5015 option — not a substitute for 5015 in wide-duct designs
Limited community configs written around 4020 blowers vs ubiquitous 5015 options
Niche use case — only relevant if your toolhead specifically calls for a 4020 blower
Name: Delta BFB0424HH 4020 Blower
Description: The Delta BFB0424HH is a 24V centrifugal blower in a compact 40×20mm footprint, suited for toolhead designs too tight for a 5015. Some Dragon Burner and XOL variants use a 4020 blower where mounting geometry prevents 5015 placement. Ball bearing construction gives it industrial longevity over generic sleeve-bearing alternatives, and Delta’s supply chain means it’s sourced through Digi-Key or Mouser rather than AliExpress.
Verdict Label: Compact 24V blower for tight toolhead layouts where a 5015 won’t fit

Pros:
- Ball bearing variant — better lifespan than standard GDStime sleeve
- Conveniently sourced alongside Trianglelab hotends and Sherpa/TBG extruders in one order
- Slightly better airflow than GDStime in community comparisons
- Competitively priced (~$6–10)
Cons:
- Trianglelab does not publish independent fan specs — performance data is community-reported
- ‘Turbo’ branding is marketing — no independent verification of claimed performance advantage
- Sunon MF50151VX is better documented and similarly priced
- AliExpress only — no distributor availability
Name: Trianglelab 5015 Turbo Blower
Description: The Trianglelab 5015 turbo blower is a common sight in builds where the builder sourced it alongside a Dragon or CHC hotend from Trianglelab. It’s a competent ball-bearing 5015 that performs better than the GDStime BOM fan. ‘Turbo’ is marketing nomenclature — the actual advantage over the Sunon MF50151VX is modest at best. Fine if it’s in a kit you’re already buying; don’t source it independently when the Sunon is available for similar money.
Verdict Label: Decent rebranded 5015 — acceptable if bundled, no reason to seek it out independently
CFM / Static Pressure: ~4.0 CFM / ~175 Pa (community estimate — no published spec)

Pros:
- Voron official BOM fan — universally specified and supported
- Extremely cheap (~$3–5 each) — stock spares without guilt
- Available from every 3D printing vendor including LDO kit suppliers
- Adequate airflow for PLA, PETG, and Flex at normal print speeds
Cons:
- Sleeve bearing has limited lifespan in enclosed, hot Voron chambers (50–60°C accelerates wear)
- Performance varies between vendor batches — buy from reputable sources
- Louder than premium alternatives at equivalent flow
- Not rated for continuous high-speed duty cycles
Name: GDStime 5015 Blower
Description: The GDStime 5015 blower is the Voron BOM default for part cooling — it works, it’s cheap, and every Voron config has been tested with one. The sleeve bearing is the primary weakness in enclosed printers where chamber temps accelerate wear. At $3–5 each it’s not worth engineering around; just keep spares. For builders wanting better reliability or quieter operation, the Sunon MF50151VX or Delta BFB0524HH are the natural next steps.
Verdict Label: Voron BOM default — functional, buy spares

Pros:
- 17.9 dBA — nearly inaudible compared to GDStime (35 dBA) or any other 4010
- SSO2 self-stabilizing oil pressure bearing: rated 150,000+ hours at 25°C
- Noctua AAO frame reduces harmonic resonance and vibration
- Includes 3-speed adapter cables (Low/Ultra-Low noise) for flexibility
- Better airflow than GDStime at lower noise levels
Cons:
- 12V operation only — 24V Voron builds require a dedicated step-down converter (DC-DC buck converter)
- ~$14–16 vs ~$3 for GDStime — 5× price for a hotend cooling fan
- Brown/beige color — not for aesthetically sensitive builds
- Many Voron mainboards (Octopus Pro, Manta M8P) lack a 12V rail, requiring an external converter
Name: Noctua NF-A4x10 FLX
Description: Noctua’s NF-A4x10 FLX is the quietest 4010 available and the standard recommendation for builders building silent machines. At 17.9 dBA it’s barely audible next to the GDStime’s 35 dBA. The SSO2 bearing delivers exceptional longevity. The catch: 24V Voron systems need a step-down converter — the community has well-documented wiring guides for this. If you’d rather run 24V natively without extra electronics, the Sanyo 9GA0412P3K001 is a strong alternative.
Verdict Label: Quietest 4010 available — needs 12V step-down on 24V Voron builds

Noise (dBA): ~65 dBA at full speed (remote mount essential)
Pros:
47 m³/h max airflow at 0 kPa
12.5 kPa max static pressure (24V) / 14 kPa (48V)
Dramatically outperforms any 5015 blower fan
3-phase brushless DC motor with NMB ball bearings
20,000+ hour MTTF
PWM speed control compatible
Available in 24V and 48V variants
Cons:
Requires remote mounting — not suitable for direct toolhead attachment
Needs a CPAP tube routed from remote location to toolhead
Adapter board or PWM controller required for Klipper control
Overkill for small-format builds like V0
Name: Wonsmart WS9290
Description: The Wonsmart WS9290 is the CPAP blower used in most remote part-cooling builds for high-performance Voron toolheads. Originally designed for medical CPAP machines, it delivers 47 m³/h airflow at 0 kPa and up to 12.5 kPa static pressure in the 24V variant. At full speed it produces substantially more airflow than any conventional 5015 blower fan, at the cost of being too large and heavy to mount on the toolhead itself.
Verdict Label: Best-in-class CPAP blower for remote high-flow builds

Noise (dBA): ~60 dBA at full speed (remote mount essential)
Pros:
- 70×40mm centrifugal motor delivers CPAP-grade airflow via hose to the toolhead
- Orders of magnitude more airflow than any 5015 blower — enables 500+ mm/s part cooling
- Brushless 3-phase motor: no brush wear, 30,000+ hour design life
- De facto VzBot community standard for part cooling
- Enables demanding overhangs and cooling at print speeds where 5015 blowers saturate
Cons:
- Must be remotely mounted — the 70×40mm motor cannot go on the toolhead
- Requires complete rethinking of toolhead cooling vs standard Voron approach
- CPAP tubing routing adds wiring complexity and aesthetic impact
- Loud (~60 dBA at speed) — enclosed printer box helps but doesn’t eliminate noise
- Not compatible with Stealthburner, XOL, or Dragon Burner without dedicated custom duct
Name: Wonsmart WS7040 CPAP Blower
Description: The Wonsmart WS7040 is the part cooling system used in VzBot and other extreme-speed platforms where conventional 5015 blowers can’t deliver enough airflow for high-speed dynamics. The 70×40mm motor mounts remotely (typically rear frame), routing air through a CPAP tube to a custom duct at the toolhead. This architecture is fundamentally different from standard Voron cooling — plan the entire toolhead and duct system together if adopting it. On VzBot it’s the established community standard and well-supported; on other platforms it requires significant custom work.
Verdict Label: VzBot’s native cooler — extreme airflow for extreme print speeds
CFM / Static Pressure: ~20+ CFM through duct / very high static pressure

Pros:
- 24V native — no step-down converter required (unlike Noctua NF-A4x10)
- Very quiet (~22 dBA) for a 24V ball-bearing axial — dramatic improvement over GDStime
- Sanyo Denki ball bearing: industrial quality, long MTTF, consistent factory specs
- Drop-in 4010 physical footprint and JST connector
- Preferred by builders who want quiet operation without voltage conversion complexity
Cons:
- More expensive than GDStime (~$12–18 vs ~$3)
- Less widely stocked at Digi-Key/Mouser than Noctua — often requires specialty stores or AliExpress listings
- Slightly higher noise floor than Noctua NF-A4x10 (22 dBA vs 17.9 dBA) — tradeoff for 24V native operation
- Part number verification important — confirm specs from seller before ordering, especially on informal AliExpress listings
Name: Sanyo 9GA0412P3K001
Description: The Sanyo Denki 9GA0412P3K001 is the community’s preferred 24V hotend cooling fan for builders wanting quiet operation without voltage conversion complexity. Running natively at 24V, it drops into any Voron fan port without modification and delivers ~22 dBA — meaningfully quieter than GDStime’s 35 dBA. Sanyo Denki manufactures for industrial and server markets; quality and batch consistency are well above AliExpress-tier alternatives. Sits slightly above the Noctua NF-A4x10 for installation convenience (24V, no converter) and slightly below it for ultimate noise floor.
Verdict Label: Best 24V hotend fan — Noctua-quiet without the step-down converter

Pros:
- Voron BOM hotend cooling fan — drop-in compatible with all major toolheads
- Very cheap (~$2–4) — trivially replaceable
- Adequate airflow for hotend cold-side cooling at standard chamber temperatures
- Universal availability from any 3D print vendor
Cons:
- Sleeve bearing degrades in enclosed Voron chamber environments
- Quality inconsistency between batches — some units whistle or vibrate
- Not suitable for sustained high-chamber-temp use without periodic replacement
- Noctua NF-A4x10 is dramatically quieter for a modest price premium
Name: Gdstime 4010 Axial
Description: The Gdstime 4010 axial is the standard hotend cooling fan for Voron builds — its job is keeping the cold zone of the hotend cold, and it does that. The sleeve bearing is the weak point in sealed enclosures where ambient temps hit 50–60°C; plan to replace it annually in heavy-use enclosed builds. At $2–3 it’s entirely disposable. Builders sensitive to noise or running hot chambers should look at the Noctua NF-A4x10 or Sanyo 9GA0412P3K001.
Verdict Label: BOM hotend cooling fan — works fine, plan to replace eventually

Pros:
- Noticeably better than GDStime based on community build comparisons
- Ball bearing variant available — better lifespan than GDStime sleeve
- Convenient to source alongside other Mellow/FLY components in a single AliExpress order
- Reasonably priced (~$8–12)
Cons:
- Mellow does not publish verified fan specs — CFM and pressure ratings are community estimates only
- Less long-term community data than Sunon or Delta
- ‘High-flow’ marketing claim unverified by independent testing
- Available only via AliExpress — no distributor channel
Name: Mellow 5015 High-Flow Blower
Description: Mellow’s 5015 high-flow blower is commonly bundled with Mellow FLY boards and Sherpa extruder kits, making it a natural pairing in the Mellow ecosystem. Community feedback puts it above GDStime in airflow consistency and build quality, but Mellow doesn’t publish specs so comparisons rely on community testing. If you’re already ordering from Mellow, it’s a sensible pick. Otherwise the Sunon MF50151VX is better validated at a similar price.
Verdict Label: Above GDStime, below Sunon in validation — fine if you’re already ordering from Mellow
CFM / Static Pressure: ~4.5 CFM / ~180 Pa (community estimate — no published spec)
